provides funding for the metropolitan transportation authority 2025-2029 capital program (Part M); establishes a demonstration program on certain covered locations to enforce vehicle weight restriction on such interstate by means of mobile or stationary weigh in motion systems (Part N); authorizes a photo monitoring program for the Triborough bridge and tunnel authority and New York state bridge authority; extends provisions relating to certain notices of liability (Part Q); relates to the effectiveness of the New York state health insurance continuation assistance demonstration project (Part S); authorizes the Olympic regional development authority to enter into agreements for membership of one or more of its ski venues in reciprocal ski pass programs where such members are required to guarantee contractual indemnity up to a capped amount (Part T); regulates artificial intelligence companion models; establishes a suicide prevention fund (Part U); relates to refund policies for online retailers (Part V); enhances disclosure requirements for automatic renewals (Part W); requires disclosure of algorithmically set prices for goods and services (Part X); relates to the regulation of buy-now-pay-later lenders; requires such lenders to be licensed or authorized; establishes prohibited acts, limitations on loans, and consumer protections (Part Y); establishes reporting requirements for pharmacy benefit managers about the rebate contracts between pharmacy benefit managers and drug manufacturers (Part Z); provides for rate increases for hire motor vehicle insurance (Part CC); extends the authority of the New York state urban development to administer the empire state economic development fund (Part EE); extends the power of the New York state urban development corporation to make loans to 07/01/2026 (Part FF); extends the authority of the dormitory authority to enter into certain design and construction management agreements (Part GG); expands certain provisions of the state finance law and the New York state infrastructure trust fund; directs a policy study analyzing ways to improve the effectiveness of the minority and women-owned business enterprise program (Part KK); increases the cap on the amount of money authorized to be on deposit pursuant to the excelsior linked deposit program at any given time (Part LL); relates to purchasing thresholds for minority- or women-owned businesses or service-disabled veteran-owned businesses (Part MM); authorizes the New York convention center operating corporation to establish a subsidiary for the purposes of forming a pure captive insurance company (Part NN); extends the waste tire management fee until December 31, 2027; requires notice of the waste tire management and recycling program to be provided to customers; removes the exclusion for mail order sales (Part PP); extends provisions of the deer hunting program to 2028 (Part QQ); relates to financial responsibility, recovery of response costs and natural resource damages, and abatement actions relating to disposal of inactive hazardous waste (Part RR); relates to the recall of a class B firefighting foam; prohibits the sale or distribution of firefighting personal protective equipment that contains intentionally added PFAS; directs the department of environmental conservation to make a recommendation to the legislature on whether to postpone the effectiveness of such provisions (Part SS); exempts conveyances of real property for open space, parks, or historic preservation purposes to any not-for-profit corporation operated for conservation, environmental, parks or historic preservation purposes (Part TT); authorizes the New York state energy research and development authority to finance a portion of its research, development and demonstration, policy and planning, Fuel NY program, climate change related expenses of the department of environmental conservation from an assessment on gas and electric corporations (Part VV); relates to utility and cable television assessments that provide funds to the department of health from cable television assessment revenues and to the department of agriculture and markets, department of state, the office of parks, recreation and historic preservation, and the department of environmental conservation from utility assessment revenues; requires accountings be submitted of such funds (Part XX); increases and redirects civil penalties for failing to comply with the department of public service's prescribed rules and regulations established for the protection of underground facilities; amends the effectiveness of certain provisions relating to establishing the underground facilities safety training account (Part YY); authorizes the department of taxation and finance to disclose certain information to the department of environmental conservation or the New York state energy research and development authority for the purpose of implementing the New York state climate leadership and community protection act (Part ZZ); establishes a commission to replace the statue of Robert R. Livingston in the National Statuary Hall of the United States Capitol with a statue of Harriet Tubman; provides that such commission shall consist of the governor or a designee, the temporary president of the senate or a designee, the speaker of the assembly or a designee, the executive director of the council on the arts or a designee, and the commissioner of the office of general services or a designee (Part BBB); extends certain rebates to municipalities for clean vehicle projects (Part CCC); relates to appointments to the cannabis board, removes provisions of law deeming a person acting as chairperson of the cannabis control board as a state officer; relates to agreements of such board with the New York state Indian nations and tribes (Part DDD); relates to a special license fee for a licensee allowed to engage in the cultivation, processing, distribution and retail of both medical cannabis and adult use cannabis; makes a conforming technical change; and provides for the repeal of certain provisions of the cannabis law (Part EEE).

325998.label: Petroleum Refineries
325998.reason: Refineries maintain AFFF-based fire suppression systems and historically ran AFFF fire-training exercises on-site -- a real, documented PFAS contamination pathway distinct from manufacturing it. (Checked live in this project's discovery pipeline for direct liability findings -- none yet; this flag is a forward-looking use-case risk, not a finding.)

325998.label: Scheduled Air Transportation
325998.reason: FAA Part 139 historically mandated AFFF-based fire suppression at certificated airports; airport authorities and some airlines have been named co-defendants in real AFFF contamination litigation.

325199.label: Textile and Fabric Finishing Mills
325199.reason: PFAS-based water/stain-repellent textile treatments (the same chemical family as 3M's Scotchgard) are a well-documented downstream use.

325199.label: Carpet and Rug Mills
325199.reason: PFAS stain-resistant carpet treatments -- the same reasoning this project already applied when curating Mohawk Industries and Dixie Group as candidate defendants (checked live, no current liability finding, but the use case itself is real and documented).

325199.label: All Other Converted Paper Product Manufacturing
325199.reason: PFAS grease-resistant food-packaging coatings -- the same reasoning already applied to Clearwater Paper.

325199.label: Toilet Preparation Manufacturing
325199.reason: PFAS use in cosmetics -- directly corroborated by a real signal already in this project's own data: California AB1603, 'Perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS): Department of Pesticide Regulation,' on record in legislative_timeline.

325199.label: Electroplating, Plating, Polishing, Anodizing and Coloring
325199.reason: PFAS used as a mist suppressant in chrome electroplating -- the same reasoning this project already used curating Honeywell International into CURATED_LIABILITY_NAICS.

pfas.reasoning: 3M's real $10.3B public water system settlement (2023) and DuPont/Chemours/Corteva's real $1.185B settlement are large, negotiated, pre-bankruptcy global settlements covering a broad share of claims -- but no curated PFAS/AFFF defendant has filed Chapter 11 over this liability as of this writing. Real personal-injury claims (15,222 in MDL 2873 as of April 2026) remain in active MDL litigation outside any bankruptcy trust.
pfas.next_stage_watch: Would move to bankruptcy_trust or bankruptcy_preemption if any curated defendant files Chapter 11 specifically over PFAS/AFFF liability -- watch the Material Event (8-K) pipeline for this; none has triggered it as of this writing.

talc.reasoning: J&J is financially solvent, not insolvent -- it has filed Chapter 11 THREE times through two different subsidiaries (LTL Management in 2021 and again in 2023 after the first was dismissed; Red River Talc in 2025) specifically to halt and consolidate MDL 2738 litigation on its own settlement terms, the real pattern academic literature calls 'bankruptcy preemption.' The third attempt was rejected by the bankruptcy court in 2025; J&J announced it will litigate individual cases instead rather than appeal, per real reporting.
talc.next_stage_watch: A fourth bankruptcy attempt, or a return to large individual jury verdicts (the real Ingham pattern -- $4.69B original verdict, reduced to ~$2.1B on appeal) if the bankruptcy route is fully abandoned, are both real possible next moves -- watch the Material Event (8-K) pipeline and JPML's own pending-actions count for signals either way.

turnout_gear.reasoning: MDL-3191 is genuinely new litigation -- JPML's own November 2026 report shows 17 pending actions and 17 total historical (pending equals total, meaning nothing has resolved yet). No curated defendant, no global settlement, and certainly no bankruptcy filing exists for this category as of this writing -- the earliest real stage in the documented progression.
turnout_gear.next_stage_watch: Watch for: a curated defendant being identified (none is yet), the first settlement disclosure in a 10-K/8-K, and the JPML pending-actions count growing past its current 17 -- any of these would be the first real sign of this MDL moving to the next stage.

glp1_weight_loss.reasoning: REPORTED: a June 2026 litigation-tracker update states plainly 'Allegations Only -- No Settlement Yet,' and real JPML numbers directly confirm this -- 4,082 pending vs 4,196 total historical actions (Nov 2026 report) is nearly a 1:1 ratio, meaning almost nothing has resolved. A related but distinct sub-MDL, MDL-3163 (GLP-1 NAION/vision-loss claims), was split off by the JPML in December 2025 -- a different claimed injury theory, not double-counted here.
glp1_weight_loss.next_stage_watch: REPORTED estimates put a global resolution 'at least one to two years away' as of mid-2026 -- speculative, not a court-scheduled date. Watch for the first bellwether trial result (none selected as of this writing) and any 8-K settlement disclosure from Novo Nordisk or Eli Lilly, neither of which is currently a curated severity-anchor defendant in this project.

paraquat.reasoning: REPORTED (secondary/law-firm sources, not a primary court document directly read): the first Parkinson's bellwether (Philadelphia state court) settled the day before trial on undisclosed terms; a federal bellwether set for October 2025 was vacated to allow settlement talks; press coverage describes a qualified settlement fund approved around March 2026 and an 'MDL Settlement Order' dated April 21, 2026, with an April 2026 bellwether also canceled. JPML's own real count (6,635 pending / 8,529 total, Nov 2026) shows a meaningful share already resolved or transferred, consistent with an active global-settlement process, though the order's actual terms were not independently confirmed here.
paraquat.next_stage_watch: Watch for a primary-source confirmation of the settlement fund's terms and opt-out mechanics (reported but unverified as of this entry), and for Syngenta/Corteva 8-K disclosures of the real settlement amount, which would let this move from REPORTED to VERIFIED.

cpap.reasoning: Philips announced a real ~$1.1B economic-loss/consumer settlement plus a separate $25M medical-monitoring settlement in April 2024, filed in the W.D. Pa. federal court, with an Aug 9 2024 claims deadline and payments expected starting 2025 (widely reported, not yet independently confirmed as fully disbursed). Important: this settlement explicitly covers ECONOMIC LOSS / consumer claims, not the separate personal-injury tort claims that remain in MDL-3014 -- JPML's real 626 pending / 1,036 total (Nov 2026) reflects those still-active personal-injury claims, a genuinely different claim population than the $1.1B figure. Flagged explicitly to avoid the same conflation mistake this project's hard rules already guard against for 3M's three distinct PFAS dollar figures.
cpap.next_stage_watch: Watch for a personal-injury-specific global settlement or bankruptcy filing, which has not occurred -- the $1.1B figure already in press coverage is NOT that.

opioid.reasoning: Mixed, real, dual-track resolution -- classified at the more consequential track: Purdue Pharma filed Chapter 11 in 2019 specifically because the opioid litigation was genuinely existential for it (unlike the solvent-company 'bankruptcy_preemption' pattern 3M/J&J used), and its real plan -- a $7.4B settlement funded substantially by the Sackler family, confirmed by the bankruptcy court in late 2025 after the Supreme Court's 2024 Harrington v. Purdue Pharma ruling forced a renegotiation of non-debtor releases -- went EFFECTIVE on May 1, 2026, with assets transferred to a new entity (Knoa Pharma LLC/Knoa Foundation). This is a genuine, completed bankruptcy_trust resolution, the canonical Manville-Trust-style pattern. Separately, most OTHER defendants (distributors McKesson/Cardinal Health/AmerisourceBergen, plus J&J) resolved via the real ~$50B National Opioid Settlement (2021-2022 multistate AG agreements) WITHOUT bankruptcy -- a global_settlement track for those defendants specifically, not conflated with Purdue's distinct bankruptcy track.
opioid.next_stage_watch: Largely resolved for the major defendants; JPML's real 2,877 pending / 3,184 total (Nov 2026) reflects remaining individual claims still working through the existing settlement/trust structures, not new unresolved liability exposure.

insulin_pbm.reasoning: Real, current, early-stage litigation -- JPML's own 516 pending / 619 total (Nov 2026 report) shows most actions are still active, not resolved. New plaintiffs are still joining: a real January 2026 filing (Park District Risk Management Agency, an Illinois public risk pool, against Eli Lilly/CVS/UnitedHealth) and Jefferson Health's early-2026 suit against insulin makers and PBMs both landed in this MDL. Important: a SEPARATE, parallel track -- the FTC's own administrative antitrust case against PBMs -- has already produced real settlements with Express Scripts (Feb 2026) and Caremark (later in 2026), but those are FTC regulatory settlements, not private MDL settlements, and are not counted in MDL-3080's own pending/total figures. Flagged explicitly to avoid conflating the two distinct legal tracks.
insulin_pbm.next_stage_watch: Watch for a global private settlement in MDL-3080 itself (distinct from the FTC's own administrative settlements, which have already happened) and for any insulin manufacturer/PBM 8-K material-event disclosure, which would be the first sign of movement toward the next stage.

earplugs.reasoning: 3M's own real press release (news.3m.com, 2023-12-27) confirms a $6B global settlement agreement reached August 29, 2023, with payments continuing through 2029 and a 98% claimant-participation threshold 3M can walk away below (though it has not). JPML's own real count -- 2 pending / 391,239 total historical (Nov 2026) -- is the most extreme resolution ratio of any MDL this project tracks, directly confirming the federal MDL itself is functionally wound down; remaining work (per secondary law-firm sources) is claims administration and payment disbursement, not active litigation.
earplugs.next_stage_watch: None expected -- this is the most fully resolved category tracked. Only a real risk would be 3M invoking the 98% walk-away clause, which would be a genuine reversal worth watching for in 3M's own 8-K filings.

ai_agent_liability_cases.legal_theory: Computer Fraud and Abuse Act (CFAA) / unauthorized computer access -- Amazon alleged Perplexity's shopping agent accessed Amazon's site on a user's behalf without authorization.
ai_agent_liability_cases.outcome_summary: The 9th Circuit's August 4, 2026 opinion held the AI agent 'is a tool, not a person' for statutory purposes, treated the human USER as the actor accessing Amazon (not Perplexity), and vacated the injunction against Perplexity on the preliminary record. Decided under computer-access law, not agency law -- the court explicitly declined to resolve who is liable when an agent acts on its own.
ai_agent_liability_cases.why_it_matters: Likely the first federal appellate ruling on a commercially deployed agentic-AI system's legal status. Real, current, and a federal docket (trackable via CourtListener once a real API token is available).

ai_agent_liability_cases.legal_theory: Employment discrimination (disparate impact) -- the theory that Workday's AI screening software functioned as an 'agent' of the hiring employers, extending discrimination liability to the AI VENDOR itself, not just the employer.
ai_agent_liability_cases.outcome_summary: A federal judge allowed the discrimination claims to proceed against Workday on the 'agent' theory -- a real, if preliminary, signal that AI vendors (not just deployers) can face direct liability for an AI system's outputs.
ai_agent_liability_cases.why_it_matters: Real federal precedent-in-progress on AI-VENDOR (not just AI-deployer) liability -- directly relevant to any insurer covering a software/AI company's E&O or tech liability line.

uk_fire_authority_risk_profile.methodology_note: Descriptive injury-rate benchmark only. The UK has no statutory firefighter cancer presumption law (IIAC has declined to prescribe it), so this is not a presumption-pricing engine -- it flags FRAs whose reported personnel-injury rate per 1,000 operational incidents is >=25% above either the England-wide benchmark or that FRA's own trailing 5-year average.

reserve_development_benchmark.methodology: Real, computed aggregate paid-loss development curves from the Casualty Actuarial Society's public 'Loss Reserving Data Pulled from NAIC Schedule P' dataset (accident years 1998-2007, compiled from real NAIC statutory filings). For each development lag N, the value is the aggregate cumulative paid loss at that lag divided by the aggregate cumulative paid loss at the latest observed lag (10) -- i.e. 'by lag N, this line of business had on average paid out this fraction of what it eventually paid.' NOT PFAS- or talc-specific; these accident years predate that litigation's real scale. Used only as a general products/liability-line benchmark for how slowly claims normally mature -- the same order-of-magnitude-analog role the RAND asbestos DCC ratio plays elsewhere in this project, never an actuarial estimate for any specific curated defendant.
